hooks.text: Hundreds of armored French knights were found suffocated without a single wound.
Why did hundreds of elite French knights drown in a plowed field?
In 1415, the world's most powerful army was defeated by mud.

title: Why Did French Knights Drown in the Mud? 🤯
description: In 1415, the French army met a shocking end in the mud of Agincourt. Discover why hundreds of elite knights suffocated without ever being struck by a sword.

beats.text: Hundreds of armored French knights were found suffocated without a single wound.
beats.visual: medieval manuscript illumination of fallen knights at the Battle of Agincourt

beats.text: In 1415, a massive French army trapped King Henry at Agincourt.
beats.visual: portrait painting of King Henry V of England

beats.text: But heavy rain had turned the plowed fields into a knee-deep swamp.
beats.visual: photograph of a muddy plowed field in the French countryside

beats.text: As the knights charged, their heavy armor became a death trap.
beats.visual: photograph of 15th-century French steel plate armor

beats.text: The ranks were so tight that men could not swing their swords.
beats.visual: medieval manuscript showing a crush of knights in battle

beats.text: Many suffocated or drowned inside their helmets within the thick muck.
beats.visual: close up photograph of a 15th-century steel bascinet helmet

better_than_last: Used the Mystery structure to frame the specific cause of death as the ultimate answer to the opening contradiction hook.
